note: Summaries, registrations, usage and the Laya wording sweep for the reranker benchmark. Comparison set: 100 random test queries per dataset. Tuning set: 50 other test queries per dataset. Local paths are shortened; raw per-request outputs are not included.

screen_manifest.retrieval: SQLite FTS5 BM25 (unicode61, OR terms) + BGE-small exact cosine, RRF constant 60
screen_manifest.truncation: Embedder and rerankers truncate at 512 tokens, as in standard BEIR runs.

laya.cohort: 100 test queries drawn with random.Random('beir-screen-20261005-scifact').sample(sorted ids, 100); same queries for every added arm.
laya.method: Decision arms: one request per passage with state {query, passage} and the registered yes/no question; rank by P(yes), ties by document ID. Luna: one request ordering all candidates.
laya.failure_policy: No retries. A failed query stays in the cohort with an empty ranking. Collection stops after three failed queries in a row.
laya.primary: laya minus minilm, nDCG@10 on the attempted queries, paired bootstrap over queries, 95% interval

luna-retry.deviation: The first run sent both datasets in parallel and 22 of 100 queries failed or were not sent (fast APIError, about 2 s each, scattered), against 2 of 120 in earlier sequential runs. This retry sends only those queries once more, sequentially. Registered after seeing which queries failed and the scores of the completed ones; no prompt or setting changed. Queries that fail again stay as failures.

luna-retry2.deviation: The first run sent both datasets in parallel and 22 of 100 queries failed or were not sent (fast APIError, about 2 s each, scattered), against 2 of 120 in earlier sequential runs. This retry sends only those queries once more, sequentially. Registered after seeing which queries failed and the scores of the completed ones; no prompt or setting changed. Queries that fail again stay as failures. Second retry: 5 queries failed again. One was re-sent by hand to read the error and the provider answered server_is_overloaded, a transient capacity error unrelated to the query. These queries are sent once more; any that still fail stay as failures.

jev-parallel.cohort: The first 20 of the 100 registered comparison queries, in registered order.
jev-parallel.method: Batched, as hosted Jev rerankers are used: the 50 candidates go in three requests of 17, 17 and 16 passages in retrieval order. Each request has state {query, passages} and one four-level rubric question per passage (the public Jev benchmark's rubric). Rank by expected level; ties by document ID. 17 per request keeps the largest request under the release's 16,384-token default. Identical request bodies to the Clef-flash arm. Timing check: identical request bodies to the jev arm, but the three requests of a query are sent at the same time.
jev-parallel.failure_policy: No retries. A failed query stays in the cohort with an empty ranking. Collection stops after three failed queries in a row.
jev-parallel.primary: Median seconds per query with three parallel requests. Not a quality comparison; rankings are compared with the sequential run only to confirm they agree.
